main: ### 1. Introduction
Kbps is a discord bot project for Slay.one, the purpose of it is improving gaming experience for players for free.
Here is the link of the project source codes - https://github.com/flashxwx/kbps
### 2. Current activity
Use `/current` command to get every server activity. (matches, real player count, top players of each match, ranked search count)
### 1. How the bot collect player activity data in Slay.one?
The bot has a program that try to get a list of every public game rooms every 60 seconds; \
And the program will manage to join each game room to watch the player activity in real time.
The program also listen to the change of search of 1v1 ranked match.
### 3. Peak activity chart
Use `/peak` command to get peak activity chart of Slay.one, you can also modify a bit the chart based on your need.
### 4. Notification of player activity
Use `/radio` command to manage the switch of radio for you, radio can work in DMs or voice channel. \
We got radio in voice and in DMs, both are off in default, you got to turn on them through buttons on `/radio` UI.
### 1. How does the radio work in DMs
After turning on radio in DMs, the bot will send you a brief report \
once there is any positive change of player activity every 30 seconds. \
And the brief report will include the activty information of all servers.
There will also be a turning off button following with the brief report for your conveniece.
### 2. How does the radio work in Voice
After turning on radio in Voice, the bot will try to join the voice channel which you are in. \
And, it will read out the brief report of any positive change of player activity every 30 seconds in voice channel. \
Same as radio in DMs, the brief report will include the activty information of all servers.
### 3. Example of brief report

`Currently, there are 0 people searching for 1v1 ranked match in Server of Europe
\

and there are 0 people searching for 1v1 ranked match in Server of America
\

and there are 0 people searching for 1v1 ranked match in Server of Asia
\

and there are 3 people playing in Server of Europe
\

and there are 0 people playing in Server of America
\
and there are 0 people playing in Server of Asia`
### 5. Replays of public games of Slay.one
Use `/replay` command to view and get the recent replays of public games.
### 1. How does the bot save replays?
The bot will watch every public games, and collect the data, and save all the game data as replay file. \
It will also save a list of players that have played in those games and some related information, so you can find out the replay you want quicker.
### 2. Limit of the space of replay saving
Currently, the maximum of the space is 5GB, which can almost save all the replay files in 4 weeks. \
It will clean up the oldest replay once it has reach the limit of the space.
### 6. External ranking for deathmatch
Use `/ranking` command to see all the rankings. Only show the first 1000 results, \
you will have to use `/rankedplayer` or `/rankedclan` to check ranks of others.
### 1. How does the ranking system work?
The system will watch all the public deathmatch, and then make out an in-game ranking base on player kills. \
And, it will calculate the win and lost of ELO scores of players at the end of every game round.

The calculation based on these criterias:
\

- Game duration
- Players' gaming duration
- In-game rank of you and your opponent (the larger gap of in-game ranks, the smaller impact)
\

- ELO score of you and your opponent (the larger gap of ELO scores, the bigger impact)
\
- Count of the match you and your opponent have played in all time (bigger change of ELO score between newbies)
### 2. Counting kills (in deathmatch)
There are two types of kills defined in the system: **Kills** & **Bot kills**. \
**Kills** include kills from guest account and player account; **Bot kills** include kills from bots and zombies.
To avoid players deliberately suicide from getting killed by others, \
the system will give kill to the player that deal damage to player who suicided in the last 5 seconds. Suicide includes deaths cause by self, bots, or zombies.
### 3. Counting duration (in deathmatch)
The gaming duration of a player is counted from the time they first join a game round until the end of the round. \
Gaming duration does NOT include death duration and leaving duration.
### 4. Clan ELO score
Clan ELO score is from ELO score that the members (who's played over 10 matches) won or lost from deathmatch. \
The ELO score that a member won will be added to clan ELO addend; \
The ELO score that a member lost will be added to clan ELO subtrahend. \
Players can contribute more to clan as their ELO score increases, \
with a bonus contribution every 100 above 1000 ELO points.
The change of clan ELO score will be caculated based on ELO addend, ELO subtrahend and the member count at that time.
### 5. Seasons of ranking
Every quarter of year is a ranking season. ELO scores of players and clans will be compressed in new season; \
The higher score, the more compression.
In new season, player kills and bot kills will be reset, same thing happen to clan ELO addend and subtrahend. \
Note that the match played count of players will not be reset.
### 6. Why didn't I find myself/others on ranking?
Possible reason 1: You haven't played at least one deathmatch since the ranking system started working.
Possible reason 2: You used the wrong server or season filter to find.
### 7. How do I avoid being ranked
For now, there's no way to make a switch for players to decide this, because of this isn't official ranking. \
You can choose to use guest account or alternate account to avoid your main account ELO score getting changed.
### 8. Formulas
Check out the python functions of formulas here: https://github.com/flashxwx/kbps/blob/main/slayone/ranking.py#L295
### 7. Ranked player information
Use `rankedplayer` to search and view ranked player information (scores, ranks, recent logs etc).
### 1. Why didn't I find a player?
Possible reason 1: You haven't played at least one deathmatch since the ranking system started working.
Possible reason 2: You used the wrong ID, nickname, or the filter of server and season to find.
### 2. Search suggestion
Input at least 3 characters, and make sure it's as accurate as possible.
### 8. Ranked clan information
Use `rankedclan` to search and view ranked clan information (scores, ranks, recent logs etc).
### 1. Why didn't I find a clan?
Possible reason 1: No one clan member had played over 10 matches since the ranking system started working.
Possible reason 2: You used the wrong clan-tag or the filter of server and season to find.
### 2. Search suggestion
Input at least 3 characters, and make sure it's as accurate as possible.
